introduction: Connecticut SNAP helps eligible households buy food with an EBT card. DSS accepts online, mailed and in-person applications.
description: Connecticut SNAP helps eligible households buy food with an EBT card. DSS accepts online, mailed and in-person applications.

sections.who: DSS assesses household composition, income and applicable student or work rules. Provide the household’s actual circumstances rather than using an old income table to rule yourself out.
sections.get: Approved households receive a monthly food benefit. Verified housing, utility, dependent-care or eligible medical expenses may affect the calculation.
sections.docs:
• Identity, Social Security number and Connecticut address records requested by DSS.
  • Recent pay stubs and other income evidence.
  • Applicable student or status records and expenses relevant to the benefit calculation.
sections.apply:
1. Submit the application

    Use the online link on DSS SNAP Apply, mail a paper form, or visit a DSS Resource Center.

  2. Send verification

    Use myDSS, the DSS Scanning Center or a resource center. Include your Client ID and Case number on mailed documents if no cover sheet is available.

  3. Complete follow-up

    DSS may call for an interview. If you have not heard after two weeks, the page lists 855-626-6632 for interview follow-up. Describe urgent food needs for expedited assessment.
sections.after: Read the decision and keep review dates. Use 211 Connecticut or Connecticut Foodshare for food while the claim is pending.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using DSS SNAP application and verification; DSS SNAP overview. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Yes. DSS lists mail and in-person options.
Use the myDSS document-submission option linked from the application page.
Eligible expenses can affect the SNAP calculation, even when they are not needed to establish basic income.
What if I need food now?
Tell DSS about the emergency and ask about expedited processing; also contact local food resources.
